messages.author: a83c43c7a0521a17
messages.subject: problems with loading Illumina HT12v4 data
parts:
Dear colleagues,
First of all, thank you for a great job you've done, your paper is really cool. I have Illumina HT12v4 data and I want to use your tool to classificate my in vitro differentiated cell lines. I'm using R 3.0.3 and I needed to download an earlier version of it (2.15.3) because otherwise "affy" version 1.36.1 which is needed for cellnetr.0.1.tar.gz wouldn't work properly. Also note that "AnnotationDbi" also needed to be installed by hands. Despite that, all the packages worked well till the moment of uploading my data. First, a warning emerged while loading sample data (I've edited your .csv file, samples IDs is 1,2,3,..) with subsequent error in the next function:
> StQuery <-expr_readSampTab ("~ / Documents / bioinf / R data / CellNet / samples_table.csv") 
Warning 
In read.table (file = file, header = header, sep = sep, quote = quote,: 
   'readTableHeader' found in the shallow end string '~ / Documents / bioinf / R data / CellNet / samples_table.csv'
> StQuery <-geo_fixNames (stQuery) 
Error in sampTab $ sample_id: $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors

And also I have an error while loading my own raw .idat files:
> ExpQuery <-Norm_cleanPropRaw (stQuery, "/ Users / mashutova / Documents / bioinf / R data / CellNet / raw_files") 
1 
Error in stTmp [, "file_name"]: incorrect number of measurements

How should they look like? Should it be one folder/.zip directory with all files? Is it possible to load .txt file with normalised values instead of .idat and analyse them directly?

Thank you in advance,
Maria

messages.subject: Re: problems with loading Illumina HT12v4 data

Hi Maria,

Thanks much for the interest, and the detailed post. Unfortunately, we have not trained CellNet on the Illumina HT12v4 platform. I have been getting a pretty good number of requests to do so. So it's possible that we will train it up for this platform. If/when we decide to do so, I will post to this group, and to the main website so that you can try it out. 

Thanks again!

Best,

Patrick
